articles.title: War dries up unofficial dollar inflows
articles.description: • Small exporters, manufacturers hit as inflows through hundi , hawala shrink sharply • Crypto investments divert billions of dollars from local market KARACHI: The country’s unaccounted foreign exchange inflows through the hundi and hawala network have declined sharply as the prolonged Gulf war disrupted Dubai’s informal trading business, hurting small exporters and domestic manufacturers. Sources in the financial sector said that hundreds of flights every year carried people with goods not registered in the official export lists to Dubai. These people are commonly known as “ khapiya ”. The Gulf war , which lasted about five months, crippled this business and also dealt a blow to the domestic manufacturing sector. “We have been preparing embroidery products for years, which were exported to the Dubai market. Now the market is closed and no buyers are available across the Gulf sta­tes,” said a manufacturer. He added that his factory is now producing only for the domestic market, which accounts for just 10 per cent of last year’s production. These businesses generated hundreds of millions of dollars, which flowed into Pakistan through illegal channels. “Apart from these businesses, the hundi and hawala system never died; it only declined. Now the Gulf war has further eroded the possibility of dollar inflows into the country through hundi or hawala ,” said a well-known currency dealer. He added that those dollars eventually found their way into Pakistan, but it was difficult to assess the volume of inflows through these informal channels. The currency market has also been reporting dollar outflows for the purchase of cryptocurrencies, with those involved in crypto trading offering up to Rs292 per dollar, compared to around Rs280 in the local market. Currency experts said several billion dollars have been invested in crypto trading, but no exact figure is available. Last year, currency dealers said Pakistanis were buying dollars from exchange companies and investing in cryptocurrencies through illegal channels, resulting in an outflow of dollars from Pakistan. “During the first 10 months of calendar year 2025, we sold about $4 billion to banks, which fell to $3bn during the same period this year. These missing dollars were mostly invested in cryptocurrencies,” said Malik Bostan, chairman of the Excha­nge Companies Association of Pakistan. He said Pakistanis buying dollars from exchange companies deposit them into their foreign currency accounts, from where they withdraw the dollars and purchase cryptocurrencies through illegal channels. However, the State Bank took initiatives to curb this outflow of dollars while, at the same time, continuing to work on developing a regulatory framework for crypto trading. In mid-April this year, Pakistan lifted its eight-year ban on crypto-related banking activity by allowing financial institutions to work with licensed virtual asset providers. The SBP issued a circular authorising regulated banks to open accounts for entities registered under the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, following the passage of the Virtual Assets Act 2026. The new framework allows banks to provide services to the sector but prohibits them from using their own capital or customer deposits to trade, hold or invest in digital assets. Published in Dawn, July 26th, 2026

articles.title: Brother Rice DL Brayden Parks is third top-10 player from Illinois headed to Irish in 2027 recruiting cycle
articles.description:
Notre Dame football’s recruiting push in Chicago continues to pay big dividends.

On Thursday, Brother Rice defensive lineman Brayden Parks announced his commitment to the Fighting Irish on CBS Sports College Football’s YouTube channel.

Parks, whose godfather is former Vocational and Notre Dame star Chris Zorich, is the third top-10 player from Illinois landed by Irish coach Marcus Freeman in the 2027 recruiting cycle.

All are from the Catholic League — St. Patrick defensive lineman David Folrunsho and Mount Carmel linebacker Roman Igwebuike are the others — and all are consensus top-200 players nationally. Parks is the No. 10 player in Illinois, the No. 24 defensive lineman and the No. 199 player nationally in the 247Sports composite rankings.

The Irish have been stocking up on local defensive linemen in recent years. Already on the roster are Simeon’s Christopher Burgess Jr., IC Catholic’s Dominik Hulak and York’s Joe Reiff.

Parks, a 6-3, 305-pounder, had more than 40 offers and cut his list of potential destinations to Notre Dame and Oregon.

He talked about his recruiting on the YouTube video: “It’s a long time coming, but at the end of the day, it’s a blessing.”

His wish list?

“I was looking for a team that’s going to be in the playoffs every year, a team that has a chance of winning a national championship.”

He also was looking for a strong connection with his coaches, who will include Freeman, defensive line coach Charlie Partridge and assistant defensive line coach Nick Sebastian.

“Just talking to coach Freeman, it shows he cares [about me], not just as a football player but as a person,” Parks said. “I’ve known coach Sebastian since I started my recruiting process about four years ago and then coach [Partridge] came into it this January.”

Parks is coming off a productive season for the Class 7A champion Crusaders. He had 61 tackles, 7œ sacks, 23 tackles for loss and an interception en route to being named Defensive Player of the Year in the rugged CCL/ESCC Blue.

National recruiting analyst Clint Cosgrove sees a bright future for Parks at Notre Dame.

“The kid is an absolute beast,” Cosgrove said. “The size/frame combination is very rare. It’s hard to find those big defensive tackles who can push those double-teams back and also rush the passer.

“He’s the complete package.”

And as good as Parks is now, Cosgrove said, “he’s just going to get bigger, better, stronger. . . . His best football is in front of him.”

More on 2027 prospects

With Parks picking Notre Dame, the vast majority of the state’s top prospects will be committed when high school practice starts Aug. 5. That doesn’t mean there won’t be any more recruiting news coming, though. In every cycle, some recruits flip schools, decommitting from one and picking another.

And there are still a few high-level prospects who haven’t made a decision. The state’s top-ranked uncommitted player in the rising senior class is No. 23 Lawrence Carr, a receiver from Kenwood.

The early signing period for football will be Dec. 4-6, with the traditional signing day scheduled for Feb. 5, 2027.
